note.text: A malapropism substitutes an inappropriate word resembling the intended word in sound, often creating an unintended comic effect. Not every spelling error or joke is a malapropism. Other confused-word errors arise from near forms, meanings or grammatical roles. Check the intended idea, the sentence pattern and a dictionary entry before choosing a correction. Sound resemblance alone does not make a replacement appropriate.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to repair a contextually wrong near-sounding word and explain the intended meaning. Builds on: lexical relationships and retelling. Leads to: accurate narrative and editing.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model error: Please give a pacific reason for changing the meeting. If the writer means an exact reason, specific is intended; pacific concerns peace. Separately, advice is a noun and advise a verb in these models: Bih gave advice; she advised the group. Correcting a word should preserve the intended message rather than merely produce a different grammatical sentence.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State what the writer seems to mean, identify the unsuitable word and propose a context-fitting form. Explain the difference in meaning or function. Mark uncertainty if the intended meaning cannot be established.

example: Every spelling mistake must be a malapropism. Correction: The taught feature involves an inappropriate sound-related word substitution.

pick.q: The writer wants an exact reason: Please give a pacific reason. Which repair fits?
e: Oceanic does not mean exact.
Peaceful changes the intended precision to peacefulness.
That reverses the request.

pick.q: Choose the verb: Please ___ the club about the change.
e: Advice is a noun here.
Advisable is an adjective.
Adviser names a person.
pick.y: After please, the request needs the base verb advise.

pick.q: Choose the noun: Bih offered useful ___.
e: Advise is the verb, not the intended noun.
Advisable is adjectival.
That phrase does not fit the stated noun pattern.
pick.y: Advice is the uncountable noun in this use.

pick.q: Choose the form meaning receive: The secretary will ___ the documents.
e: Except ordinarily expresses exclusion here, not receipt.
Acceptance is a noun, not the base verb after will.
Exception names an excluded case.
pick.y: The intended action is acceptance, not exclusion.
